references.text: Also describes living raw flesh as a sign of impurity in connection with skin disease.
The preceding verse explains that when raw flesh appears, the person is unclean.
The continuation describing what happens if the raw flesh turns white again and the person is declared clean.
The priest's role in examining and declaring a person unclean due to skin disease.
Describes the priest's role in examining lepers and declaring them clean or unclean.
Miriam is struck with leprosy, described as white as snow, related to צָרַעַת (tsara'at).
Exhortation to follow the priests' instructions regarding leprosy.
Naaman's leprosy passes to Gehazi, an example of צָרַעַת in a historical context.
Jesus heals a leper and sends him to the priest to show himself clean, in accordance with the Mosaic Law.
Jesus sends the ten lepers to the priests to be declared clean, referring to Leviticus' purity regulations.
